body: The prostate is a small gland below the bladder. It can enlarge with age, become inflamed, or need evaluation when PSA is abnormal.
Common prostate problems include benign prostate enlargement, prostatitis, urine flow problems, urinary retention, and prostate cancer screening concerns.

subsections.title: Symptoms
body: Symptoms may include weak urine flow, slow starting, straining, frequent urination, night urination, urgency, incomplete emptying, burning urine, pelvic pain, or blood in urine.
Some men have no symptoms but need review because of an abnormal PSA test or abnormal scan.

subsections.title: When to consult a urologist
body: Consult a urologist if urine flow is weak, symptoms disturb sleep, urine stops suddenly, infections repeat, or medicines are not helping.
You should also consult if PSA is high, prostate feels abnormal on examination, or there is blood in urine.

subsections.title: Diagnosis and tests
body: Tests may include urine test, urine culture, PSA, ultrasound, uroflowmetry, post-void residual urine check, prostate examination, MRI prostate, or biopsy when needed.
The aim is to know whether symptoms are due to enlargement, infection, blockage, cancer risk, or another cause.

experience.title: Treatment options for prostate problems
body: Treatment depends on symptoms, prostate size, urine flow, infection, PSA, and overall health.
Options may include medicines, lifestyle changes, antibiotics for infection, catheter support, endoscopic surgery, laser surgery, or cancer workup.

careGuide.note: Your plan will depend on symptoms, PSA, prostate size, infection risk, and test results.

items.question: Does enlarged prostate mean cancer?
items.answer: No. Benign prostate enlargement is common. PSA, examination, and tests help assess cancer risk.

items.question: When is prostate surgery needed?
items.answer: Surgery may be needed when medicines do not help, urine retention occurs, infections repeat, or blockage affects the bladder or kidneys.

items.question: Is high PSA always cancer?
items.answer: No. PSA can rise due to enlargement, infection, recent procedures, or cancer. It needs proper review.

items.question: Can medicines improve urine flow?
items.answer: Many men improve with medicines. Some still need a procedure if blockage is severe.

items.question: How often should PSA be checked?
items.answer: PSA follow-up depends on age, risk, symptoms, and previous results.
